candidate.statement: The Female King of Colonial Nigeria concerns Ahebi Ugbabe, an Igbo woman who became king in colonial Nigeria; she was exiled from Igboland, traveled widely, learned to speak many languages, and became a close companion of Nigerian Igala kings and British officers who supported her claim to the offices of headman, warrant chief, and later king.

facts.statement: The source title is 'The Female King of Colonial Nigeria'.
The source author is Nwando Achebe.
The source was published in February 2011.
Ahebi Ugbabe was an Igbo woman.
Ahebi Ugbabe became king in colonial Nigeria.
Ugbabe learned to speak many languages.
Ugbabe became a close companion of Nigerian Igala kings.
Ugbabe became a close companion of British officers.
The British officers supported Ugbabe's claim to the office of headman, warrant chief, and later, king.
Achebe traces the roots of Ugbabe's rise to fame and fortune.
Achebe provides critical perspectives on women, gender, sex and sexuality, and the colonial encounter.
Achebe considers how it was possible for this woman to take on the office and responsibilities of a traditionally male role.
